title: How do I prevent automatic updates?
creator: ron197
content:
A few weeks ago my installation of Thunderbird on my Windows 10 laptop was version 151. I want to stop it from being updated, and I asked AI for help. It suggested the following:

1. Create a directory named "distribution" and locate it as follows: C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\distribution. 2. Within that directory, I was asked to create a file named "policies.json" and I did so. 3. Within that file, I was asked to place the following: { 

 "policies": {       "DisableAppUpdate": true    }

} and that's what I did.

When I had a look under Settings > Update, there was a note to say that updates have been prevented by the administrator. (That would have been the effect of what I just did.) That was a few weeks ago.

So, when I looked at my version number today, I saw that my version is now 152. It had updated, and the directory and file I created are now no longer present.

It seems that the update process deletes anything that shouldn't be there and doesn't trouble itself with the file I created.

How do I stop Thunderbird from updating my installation?

title: macOS System Print Dialog bypasses "Open in Preview" and "Save as PDF" in Thunderbird v152 (macOS Tahoe / Apple M4)
creator: michel70
content:
Hello,

I am experiencing a severe issue with the macOS system print dialog handling in Thunderbird, which started immediately after updating to version 152.

Environment 

   * OS: macOS Tahoe 15.5.1 (26.5.1)    * Hardware: Apple M4 (Silicon)    * Thunderbird Version: 152 (Issue present) / 151 (Works perfectly)

Description of the problem: When I use the native macOS system print dialog within Thunderbird and select either "Open in Preview", Instead of opening the Preview app Thunderbird bypasses the command and immediately sends the document directly to the default physical printer. The same happens with "Save as PDF", the file-saving dialog is first presented, but after entering the filename the document is also sends to the default physical printer rather than being saved.

Steps to reproduce: 

  * Open an email in Thunderbird v152.   * Select Print...   * in the Print Dialog window, select "Print using the system dialog"    * The system print dialog is opened   * Click the PDF dropdown and select "Open in Preview" or "Save as PDF". 
  Result: The document is instantly printed on the physical printer instead of performing the macOS system action.

Steps taken: 

  * Tested with Thunderbird v151: The macOS system print dialog works perfectly as intended.   * Upgraded to v152: The issue appears immediately and consistently.   * All other applications (Safari, Chrome, Microsoft products, Apple Mail) work correctly

This seems to be a serious regression in how Thunderbird v152 handles native macOS print system events and dialog actions on Apple Silicon / macOS Tahoe.

Any help or a fix for this would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards, Michel

title: Moving TBird Archives to Local Folders, Part 2

content:
I would like to follow up on a query I posted earlier this year at https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1565806

Briefly, I want to move some more prior years' archived folders and messages to TBird's Local Folders. My effort to simply drag and drop the archive to the new location ran into trouble because (as I understand) the archive flag was not turned off in the move, leading to anomalous results. Is there a standard approved way to move archived messages to local folders, or should I just drag and drop and de-flag again?

From my earlier query: > Installing the folder flags add-on showed me (as you said) that 2024 was flagged as an archive. I turned the flag off, restarted TBird and 2024 now comes after 2023 as it should. I expect I created the problem somehow when I moved the 2024 folder from the server to Local Folders; what is the proper way to do that?
